Orthopedic Trauma definition

  • Orthopedic Trauma refers to injuries to bones, joints, ligaments, tendons caused by falls, motor vehicle accidents and sports.
  • Orthopedic Trauma includes medical and surgical management of those injuries.

Fracture definition

  • Fracture is a break or crack in the continuity of the bone, Can occur in any part of any bone
  • Results in:
  • pain
  • swelling
  • deformity
  • instability
  • change in sensibility
  • loss of function

Other definitions

  • Ligament is tissue connects bone with another bone while tendon connect muscle with a bone.
  • Dislocation is movement of a bone from its normal position in its joint, due to stretch or tear of the ligaments and other structures holding the joint.
  • Subluxation is partial dislocation of a bone within its joint.
  • Sprain is ligamentous injury.
  • Strain is injury to a tendon or to a muscle.

Bone types

  • Cortical bone
  • Compact, dense, strong
  • Found in the outer layer of the shafts of long bones, outer surface of flat bones such as skull, ribs and pelvis (80% of adult skeleton)
  • Slow turnover rate (slower healing)
  • Cancellous bone
  • Trabecular, spongy, weaker than cortical bone
  • Found in the ends of long bones and inner layer of their shafts and in the vertebral bodies, also found in inner layer of skull, ribs and pelvic bones (20% of adult skeleton)
  • High turnover rate (faster healing)
